blocks.x: Agentic AI & Hyperautomation applied to Omnichannel Retail. This page sets out the operating context, the delivery pattern we run, the services and platforms involved, and the outcomes we commit to.

Omnichannel retail wins on promise-keeping: availability, delivery promise, price consistency and service resolution across channels. The decision infrastructure behind those promises — demand sensing, allocation, pricing — decides margin before marketing spends a cent.

items: Store/DC allocation on legacy rules; phantom availability coexists with overstock.
Forecasts update weekly while baskets shift daily; markdowns and stockouts both inherit the lag.

blocks.x: The pattern composes Hyperautomation & Systems Integration, Digital Workforce & Multi-Agent Orchestration, Hyperautomation & Systems Integration from the Agentic AI & Hyperautomation tower, wired into the unit's workflows (Demand sensing and pricing, Allocation/replenishment, Order promise and fulfillment) on Dataq Swarm and Dataq Nexus and Dataq Compass. Governance inherits the sector frame — GDPR/CCPA among others — with evidence generated by the delivery itself.

items: Agents that execute the work: tool-using, policy-bounded, and fully logged for audit.
Agents operated as one fleet: roles, queues, budgets and audit trails.
Decision paths that run in milliseconds, with policy checks and full logging.
Size-curve and DC logic proposed to planners (OOS and overstock both down)

blocks.x: At industry level, the same pattern

At Retail & Consumer Goods level this capability reads as: PO changes, OTIF misses and forecast revisions orchestrated with supplier portals (email chains replaced by governed events). The sub-industry page narrows it to the unit's workflows, regimes and KPIs.

Delivery follows the same weekly rhythm on every program of this type. Weeks 1–2 lock the baseline: the current metric is measured with your team and signed before build starts. Weeks 3–8 deliver the pilot on bounded scope — one decision path, one workflow, one plant or one portfolio — with a control owner named on your side. Weeks 9–12 industrialize what worked: runbooks, monitoring, enablement and a measured delta against the signed baseline. Anything that misses its gate is stopped or redirected with a documented decision, not quietly extended.
